His words: ﴿بِيَدَيَّ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ﴾: the readers agree on the dual. Had a reader read ﴿بيدِى﴾, meaning a single hand, it would have been correct [Translator's note: the source prints «صَداباً», a misprint for «صواباً» "correct"]; as the poet says:
أيها المبتغى فناء قريشٍ * بيد الله عُمرهَا والفناء
(O you who seek the destruction of Quraysh: in the hand of Allah are its life and its destruction.)
The single one of these suffices for the two; likewise the two eyes, the two legs and the two hands: one of them suffices for the other, because their meaning is one.

farraa:84-84.t:
His words: ﴿قَالَ فَٱلْحَقُّ وَٱلْحَقَّ أَقُولُ﴾: al-Ḥasan and the people of the Hijaz read the accusative in both. Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim — and greater than them, Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid — read the nominative in the first and the accusative in the second.
Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Bihrām related to me — he was an elder who taught the Quran in the Mosque of al-Maṭmūra and the Mosque of the Shaʿbīs — from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Mujāhid, that he read (فالحقُّ منى والحقَّ أقولُ) ("the truth is from Me, and the truth I say"), i.e. "and I say the truth". That is one option; and its nominative may be by implying: "so it is the truth".
It is mentioned of Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "I am the Truth, and I say the truth." Its nominative may also be by interpreting [what follows] as its answer, because the Arabs say: al-ḥaqqu la-aqūmanna ("the truth is, I will certainly stand"), and they say: ʿazmatun ṣādiqatun la-ātiyannaka ("a firm resolve: I will certainly come to you"), because it bears the interpretation: "a firm resolve that I will come to you".
This is made clear by His words: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ﴾; do you not see that His words ﴿بَدَا لَهُمْ﴾ must have an implied nominative, so in meaning it may be nominative or accusative. The Arabs recite the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فقلتُ يَمينُ الله أبرحُ قاعداً * ولو قطَّعوا رَأْسِى لديكَ وَأوصَالى
(I said: "By the oath of Allah, I will not cease sitting here, even if they cut off my head and my limbs beside you.")
The accusative in yamīn is more frequent. The nominative is on what I have told you about implying (an), and on your saying: ʿalayya yamīnun ("an oath is upon me"). They recited to us:
فإنّ علىّ اللهَ إنْ يحملوننى * عَلَى خُطّة إلا انطلقت أَسيرها
(For I owe it to Allah: if they put me to some plan, I will set out and carry it through.)
and it is also transmitted: lā yaḥmilūnanī.
If you dropped inna, you would say: ʿalayya Allāhu la-aḍribannaka, i.e. this oath is upon me. And it may be: ʿalayya Allāhu an aḍribaka, making (Allāh) nominative by the answer. Making it nominative by ʿalā is dearer to me. Whoever makes (al-ḥaqqa wa-l-ḥaqqa) accusative does so in the sense of your saying: ḥaqqan la-ātiyannaka ("truly, I will come to you"); the alif and lām and their omission are the same. It is like your saying ḥamdan li-llāh and al-ḥamda li-llāh. And had someone put the first al-ḥaqq in the genitive, making it Allah the Exalted — I mean in the i'rab — and swearing by it, it would have been correct. The Arabs drop the wāw of the oath and keep the genitive; we have heard them say: Allāhi la-tafʿalanna ("By Allah, you will certainly do [it]"), and / 165 ب the one answering says: Allāhi la-afʿalanna ("By Allah, I will certainly do [it]"), because the meaning is in common use, and in what is commonly used omission is permitted; as one says to a man: "How are you this morning?" and he says: "khayrin" ("well"), meaning bi-khayrin; since it was frequent in speech, [the preposition] was omitted.

farraa:88-88.t:
His words: ﴿وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ﴾: the tidings of the Quran, that it is true, and the tidings of Muḥammad, peace be upon him, that he is a prophet.
His words: ﴿بَعْدَ حِينِ﴾: He says: after death, and before it: when the matter became manifest they knew it, and whoever died knew it with certainty.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿كتاب أنزلناه إليك مبارك ليدبروا آياته وليتذكر أولو الألباب﴾: (كتاب): khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a Book"; the clause ﴿أنزلناه﴾ is an adjective; (أنزل): past verb, ﴿نا﴾: fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إليك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلناه﴾; (مبارك): a second naʿt (adjective), or a second khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; (ليدبروا): the lām is the lām of purpose (lām al-taʿlīl), and (يدبروا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the lām of purpose, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from «أن» and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿أنزلناه﴾; (آياته): mafʿūl bihi; (وليذكر): conjoined to (ليدبروا) [Translator's note: the source writes «وليذكر» here, whereas the ayah reads ﴿وليتذكر﴾]; (أولو): fāʿil; and (الألباب): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿ووهبنا لداود سليمان نعم العبد إنه أواب﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (وهبنا): past verb and fāʿil (agent); ﴿لداود﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وهبنا﴾; (سليمان): object; the clause ﴿ووهبنا لداود...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (نعم): an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise, and (العبد) is its fāʿil; the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted because it was mentioned before, i.e. "he"; ﴿إنه أواب﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), the hāʾ is its noun, and (أواب) is its khabar (predicate); the clause gives the reason for the praise.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t: ﴿إذ عرض عليه بالعشي الصافنات الجياد﴾: (إذ): a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (اذكر); the clause ﴿عرض﴾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation; (عرض): passive past verb; ﴿عليه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عرض﴾; ﴿بالعشي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being at that time"; (الصافنات): nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (الجياد): a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).

muyesser-irab:32-32.t: ﴿فقال إني أحببت حب الخير عن ذكر ربي حتى توارت بالحجاب﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (قال): past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); (إن) is an abrogating particle, the yāʾ is its noun, and the clause (أحببت) is its khabar (predicate); (حب): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أحببت﴾, or standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); (الخير): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿عن ذكر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أحببت﴾; ﴿ربي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the annexation is the annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its object, i.e. "from my remembering my Lord", or to its agent, i.e. "from my Lord's remembering me"; (حتى): a particle of limit and genitive; (توارت): past verb, and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it/she" (هي); and (بالحجاب): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿توارت﴾.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t: ﴿ردوها علي فطفق مسحا بالسوق والأعناق﴾: (ردوها): imperative verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the speech (maqūl) of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "he said: Return them"; (عليّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ردوها﴾; (فطفق): conjoined to something omitted, i.e. "so they returned them"; (طفق): a past verb among the verbs of commencing (afʿāl al-shurūʿ), which operate as kāna operates, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو); (مسحًا): mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "he began wiping (يمسح) a wiping", and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of (طفق); (بالسوق): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مسحًا﴾; and (الأعناق): conjoined to (بالسوق).

muyesser-irab:34-34.t: ﴿ولقد فتنا سليمان وألقينا على كرسيه جسدا ثم أناب﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the lām occurs in the answer to an implied (muqaddar) oath; (قد): a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (فتنا): verb and fāʿil (agent); (سليمان): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿ولقد فتنا سليمان﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (ألقينا): conjoined to (فتنا); (على كرسيه): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ألقينا﴾, and the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (جسدًا): mafʿūl bihi; and (ثم أناب): also conjoined.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿قال رب اغفر لي وهب لي ملكا لا ينبغي لأحد من بعدي﴾: (رب): the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted; (هب): a verb of supplication; (لي): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) it; (ملكًا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿لا ينبغي﴾ is an adjective of (ملكًا); (لأحد): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينبغي﴾; and ﴿من بعدي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of (أحد).
﴿إنك أنت الوهاب﴾: the clause gives the reason for the supplication for forgiveness and the gift; (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), and the kāf is its noun; (أنت): a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الوهاب): khabar (predicate) of (إن), or khabar of (أنت), and [in that case] the clause is the khabar of (إن).

muyesser-irab:36-36.t: ﴿فسخرنا له الريح تجري بأمره رخاء حيث أصاب﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (سخرنا): verb and fāʿil (agent); (له): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سخرنا﴾; (الريح): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿تجري بأمره﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الريح); (تجري): imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); (بأمره): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجري﴾; (رخاء): a ḥāl from the pronoun in (تجري); (حيث): an adverb attached to ﴿تجري﴾; the clause ﴿أصاب﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; and (أصاب): past verb, and the fāʿil is latent.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t: ﴿والشياطين كل بناء وغواص﴾: the wāw: a conjunction; (الشياطين): conjoined to (الريح); (كل): a badal (substitute) from (الشياطين); (بناء): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (غواص): conjoined to (بناء).

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿وآخرين مقرنين في الأصفاد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (آخرين): conjoined to ﴿كل بناء﴾, being included with it in the ruling of the badal (substitute), and it is a badal of the whole from the whole; (مقرنين): a naʿt (adjective) of (آخرين), i.e. some of them were bound together with others in fetters; and (في الأصفاد): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مقرنين).

muyesser-irab:39-39.t: ﴿هذا عطاؤنا فامنن أو أمسك بغير حساب﴾: the clause is the speech (maqūl) of an omitted verb of saying; (هذا): mubtadaʾ (subject); (عطاؤنا): khabar (predicate), and ﴿نا﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (فامنن): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and (امنن) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); ﴿أو﴾: a conjunction of choice; (أمسك): imperative verb conjoined to (امنن); and (بغير): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عطاؤنا﴾, or attached to ﴿امنن﴾, or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from what precedes.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿وإن له عندنا لزلفى وحسن مآب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (إن): an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters); (له): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (عندنا): an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and ﴿نا﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (زلفى): the noun of (إن); (حسن): conjoined to (زلفى); and (مآب): muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿واذكر عبدنا أيوب إذ نادى ربه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (اذكر): imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (عبدنا): the object of (اذكر), and ﴿نا﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أيوب): a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of (عبدنا); (إذ): a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from (أيوب); the clause ﴿نادى﴾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "he" (هو); (ربه): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أني مسني الشيطان بنصب وعذاب﴾: (أن) is an abrogating particle, the yāʾ is its noun, and the clause (مسني الشيطان) is its khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from (أن) and what falls within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with [the words]: that Satan has touched me"; ﴿مسني الشيطان﴾: past verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil; ﴿بنصب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مسني﴾; and (عذاب): conjoined to (نصب).

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿اركض برجلك هذا مغتسل بارد وشراب﴾: the clause is the speech (maqūl) of an omitted verb of saying; (اركض): imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (برجلك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اركض﴾, and the object of (اركض) is omitted, i.e. "the ground"; (هذا): mubtadaʾ (subject); (مغتسل): khabar (predicate); (بارد): an adjective of (مغتسل); and (شراب): conjoined.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿ووهبنا له أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة منا وذكرى لأولي الألباب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (وهبنا): verb and fāʿil (agent); (له): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وهبنا﴾; (أهله): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (مثلهم): conjoined to (أهله); ﴿معهم﴾: an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being with them"; (رحمة): mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); (منا): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of (رحمة); (ذكرى): conjoined to (رحمة); (لأولي): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (ذكرى); and (الألباب): muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿وخذ بيدك ضغثا فاضرب به ولا تحنث﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (خذ): imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); (بيدك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خذ﴾; (ضغثًا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (فاضرب): conjoined to (خذ); (به): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿اضرب﴾, and the object is omitted, i.e. "your wife"; (ولا تحنث): the wāw is a conjunction, (لا) is prohibitive, and (تحنث) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا).
﴿إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), ﴿نا﴾ is its noun, and the clause ﴿وجدناه﴾ is its khabar (predicate); (وجد) is a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil, the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi, and (صابرًا) is the second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿نعم العبد﴾: verb and fāʿil, and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted because it is known, i.e. "he"; ﴿إنه أواب﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle, the hāʾ is its noun, and (أواب) is its khabar; the clause gives the reason for praising him.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿واذكر عبادنا إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب أولي الأيدي والأبصار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (اذكر): imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (عبادنا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ﴿نا﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إبراهيم): a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); ﴿وإسحاق ويعقوب﴾: conjoined to (إبراهيم); (أولي): mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: so in the source; (أولي) is ordinarily parsed as a naʿt or badal of (عبادنا)]; (الأيدي): muḍāf ilayhi; and (الأبصار): conjoined to (الأيدي).

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿إنا أخلصناهم بخالصة ذكرى الدار﴾: the clause gives a reason; (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), ﴿نا﴾ is its noun, and the clause ﴿أخلصناهم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (بخالصة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أخلصناهم﴾; (بخالصة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أخلصناهم﴾ [Translator's note: this sentence is repeated in the source]; (ذكرى): a badal (substitute) from (خالصة); (الدار): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the annexation of (ذكرى) to (الدار) is the annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its object, i.e. "their remembering the Abode of the Hereafter".

muyesser-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وإنهم عندنا لمن المصطفين الأخيار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; (عندنا): an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿من المصطفين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of (إن); and (الأخيار): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t: ﴿واذكر إسماعيل واليسع وذا الكفل وكل من الأخيار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿اذكر إسماعيل﴾: verb, latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿واليسع وذا الكفل﴾: both conjoined to (إسماعيل); (كل): mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿من الأخيار﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿هذا ذكر وإن للمتقين لحسن مآب﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; (هذا): mubtadaʾ (subject); (ذكر): khabar (predicate); (وإن): the wāw is resumptive, and (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters); (للمتقين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar of (إن); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (حسن): the postponed noun of (إن); (مآب): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause ﴿وإن للمتقين...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t: ﴿جنات عدن مفتحة لهم الأبواب﴾: (جنات): a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of (حسن مآب); (عدن): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (مفتحة): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (جنات عدن), and what governs it is the verbal sense contained in (المتقين); (لهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مفتحة); and (الأبواب): nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (مفتحة), because it is a passive participle, or a badal from the pronoun in (مفتحة), which is the pronoun of the Gardens.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t: ﴿متكئين فيها يدعون فيها بفاكهة كثيرة وشراب﴾: (متكئين): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in (لهم), and what governs it is (مفتحة); (فيها): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿متكئين﴾; the clause ﴿يدعون﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position, or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (فيها): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of (يدعون), i.e. "settled in it"; (بفاكهة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يدعون﴾; (كثيرة): an adjective; and (شراب): conjoined to (فاكهة).

muyesser-irab:52-52.t: ﴿وعندهم قاصرات الطرف أتراب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿هم﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قاصرات): postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (الطرف): muḍāf ilayhi; and (أتراب): an adjective of (قاصرات).

muyesser-irab:53-53.t: ﴿هذا ما توعدون ليوم الحساب﴾: (هذا): the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (ما): khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿توعدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. (ليوم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿توعدون﴾, and the lām is for cause, i.e. "for the sake of the Day of Reckoning"; and (الحساب): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿إن هذا لرزقنا ما له من نفاد﴾: (إن): an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters); (هذا): its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (رزقنا): khabar (predicate) of (إن); (ما): negating; (له): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar; (من): a connective (ṣila) preposition [i.e. redundant]; and (نفاد): postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) in position, genitive (majrūr) in form by ﴿من﴾.

muyesser-irab:55-55.t: ﴿هذا وإن للطاغين لشر مآب﴾: (هذا): a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "this is as mentioned", or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is this"; the statement is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the wāw is a conjunction; (إن): an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters); (للطاغين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar of (إن); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (شر): the postponed noun of (إن); and (مآب): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:56-56.t: ﴿جهنم يصلونها فبئس المهاد﴾: a badal (substitute) from (شر مآب), or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it; the clause (يصلونها) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and it is an imperfect verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and ﴿ها﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); or (جهنم) is the object of an omitted verb indicated by (يصلونها); the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you wish to know the reality of Hell, then it is a wretched resting place"; (بئس) is an inflexible (jāmid) verb for expressing blame, (المهاد) is the fāʿil, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "it" (هي).

muyesser-irab:57-57.t: ﴿هذا فليذوقوه حميم وغساق﴾: (هذا): mubtadaʾ (subject). The fāʾ is parenthetical. The lām: the lām of command. (يذوقوه): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command. The wāw: fāʿil (agent). The hāʾ: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause ﴿فليذوقوه﴾ is parenthetical, a clause with no grammatical position. (حميم): khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (غساق): conjoined, nominative (marfūʿ).

muyesser-irab:58-58.t: ﴿وآخر من شكله أزواج﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (آخر): conjoined to ﴿حميم وغساق﴾; ﴿من شكله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (آخر); and (أزواج): khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are pairs".

muyesser-irab:59-59.t: ﴿هذا فوج مقتحم معكم لا مرحبا بهم إنهم صالو النار﴾: the clause is the speech (maqūl) of an omitted verb of saying; (هذا): mubtadaʾ (subject); (فوج): khabar (predicate); (مقتحم): an adjective of (فوج); (معكم): an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second adjective of (فوج), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (فوج); (لا) is negating; (مرحبًا): accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun); ﴿بهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مرحبًا﴾; the negated clause is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position, or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), ﴿هم﴾ is its noun, and ﴿صالو﴾ is its khabar, the nūn having been dropped because of the annexation; and (النار): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:60-60.t: ﴿قالوا بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم أنتم قدمتموه لنا فبئس القرار﴾: (قالوا): verb and fāʿil (agent); (بل): a particle of digression (iḍrāb); (أنتم): mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "more deserving of the saying"; (لا) is negating; (مرحبًا): accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun); ﴿بكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مرحبًا﴾; the clause ﴿قالوا بل أنتم...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (أنتم): mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿قدمتموه﴾ is the khabar; (قدمتموه): past verb, the tāʾ is the fāʿil, the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural, the wāw is for lengthening the ḍamma of the mīm, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لنا): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدَّم﴾; (فبئس): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (بئس) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; (القرار): fāʿil; and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "the Fire".

muyesser-irab:61-61.t: ﴿قالوا ربنا من قدم لنا هذا فزده عذابا ضعفا في النار﴾: (قالوا): verb and fāʿil (agent); (ربنا): the one addressed (munādā), annexed, with the vocative particle omitted; (من): a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿قدم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) [Translator's note: so in the source; the khabar is stated below to be the clause ﴿فزده﴾, while ﴿قدم﴾ is the ṣila of (من)]; (قدم): past verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); (لنا): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قدم﴾; (هذا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa) because of the scent of condition in the relative; the clause ﴿فزده﴾ is the khabar; the verb of supplication is indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you" (أنت), and the hāʾ is in the position of the accusative as the first mafʿūl bihi; (عذابًا): second mafʿūl bihi; (ضعفًا): a naʿt (adjective) of (عذاب), i.e. "doubled"; and (في النار): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, i.e. "so increase him, being in the Fire", or a second naʿt of (عذاب).

muyesser-irab:62-62.t: ﴿وقالوا ما لنا لا نرى رجالا كنا نعدهم من الأشرار﴾: (قالوا): verb and fāʿil (agent); (ما): an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (لنا): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿لا نرى﴾ is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لا): negating; (نرى): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the fāʿil of (نرى) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we" (نحن); (رجالًا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿كنا﴾: (كان) is a deficient past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿كنا﴾ is an adjective of (رجالًا); the clause ﴿نعدهم﴾ is the khabar of (كان); and (من الأشرار): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نعدهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:63-63.t: ﴿أتخذناهم سخريا أم زاغت عنهم الأبصار﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī), and the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) has dropped, being dispensed with; (اتخذناهم): past verb, fāʿil (agent) and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (سخريًّا): second mafʿūl bihi; (أم): it is the connected «أم» (umm al-muttaṣila), a conjunction; ﴿زاغت عنهم الأبصار﴾: verb and fāʿil; (عنهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿زاغت﴾; and the clause ﴿اتخذناهم﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:64-64.t: ﴿إن ذلك لحق تخاصم أهل النار﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), and (ذلك) is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (حق): khabar (predicate) of (إن); (تخاصم): a badal (substitute) from (حق), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it" (هو); (أهل): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and it is itself muḍāf; (النار): muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause of the omitted mubtadaʾ and its khabar ﴿هو تخاصم﴾ is resumptive by way of explanation (bayāniyya), a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:65-65.t: ﴿قل إنما أنا منذر وما من إله إلا الله الواحد القهار﴾: (قل): imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); (إنما): the restraining and restrained [particle] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (أنا): mubtadaʾ (subject); (منذر): khabar (predicate); the wāw: a conjunction; (ما): negating; (من): a connective (ṣila) preposition [i.e. redundant]; (إله): genitive (majrūr) in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position as the subject of the nominal sentence (bi-l-ibtidāʾ); (إلا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); the Name of Majesty: khabar; and ﴿الواحد القهار﴾: two adjectives of «الله».

muyesser-irab:66-66.t: ﴿رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار﴾: (رب): a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty in the previous ayah, or a badal (substitute); (السماوات): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الأرض): conjoined, genitive (majrūr); (ما): a relative noun, conjoined, in the position of the genitive; (بينهما): an accusative (manṣūb) adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿العزيز الغفار﴾: also two naʿts of the Name of Majesty in the previous ayah.

muyesser-irab:67-67.t: ﴿قل هو نبأ عظيم﴾: (قل): imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿هو﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); (نبأ): khabar (predicate); and (عظيم): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:68-68.t: ﴿أنتم عنه معرضون﴾: the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of (النبأ), or resumptive, with no grammatical position; (أنتم): mubtadaʾ (subject); (عنه): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿معرضون﴾; and (معرضون): khabar (predicate) of (أنتم).

muyesser-irab:69-69.t: ﴿ما كان لي من علم بالملأ الأعلى إذ يختصمون﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; (ما): negating; (كان): a deficient past verb (one of kāna and its sisters); (لي): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (من): a connective (ṣila) preposition [i.e. redundant]; (علم): genitive (majrūr) in form by (من), in the position of the nominative as the postponed noun of (كان); (بالملأ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (علم) on the assumption of an implied muḍāf, i.e. "of the tidings of the Exalted Assembly and their disputing"; (الأعلى): an adjective of (الملأ); (إذ): an adverb for past time, attached to an omitted [noun] annexed to (الملأ), i.e. "any knowledge of the speech of the Exalted Assembly", or a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of the accusative by the maṣdar (verbal noun) ﴿علم﴾; and the clause ﴿يختصمون﴾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation.

muyesser-irab:70-70.t: ﴿إن يوحى إلي إلا أنما أنا نذير مبين﴾: (إن): negating; (يوحى): imperfect verb, built for that whose agent is not named [i.e. passive]; (إليّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يوحى﴾; (إلا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (إنما): the restraining and restrained [particle] (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and together with what it governs it has taken the place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (يوحى), i.e. "nothing is revealed to me except the warning", and the restriction is relative (iḍāfī); (أنا): mubtadaʾ (subject); (نذير): khabar (predicate); and (مبين): a naʿt (adjective). [Translator's note: the source writes «إنما» here, whereas the ayah reads ﴿أنما﴾.]

muyesser-irab:71-71.t: ﴿إذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من طين﴾: (إذ): a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from ﴿إذ يختصمون﴾, or in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (اذكر); the clause ﴿قال ربك﴾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation; ﴿قال ربك﴾: verb and fāʿil (agent); ﴿للملائكة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾. ﴿إني خالق بشرًا﴾: (إن) and what follows it is the speech (maqūl) of the saying; (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), the yāʾ is its noun, and (خالق) is its khabar (predicate); (بشرًا): mafʿūl bihi of (خالق); and (من طين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿بشرًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:72-72.t: ﴿فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين﴾: the fāʾ: a conjunction; (إذا): an adverb of future time that puts its condition in the genitive and is made accusative by its apodosis (jawāb); ﴿سويته﴾: past verb, the tāʾ: fāʿil (agent), the hāʾ: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (نفخت): conjoined to (سويته); (فيه): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نفخت﴾, and likewise His words ﴿من روحي﴾; ﴿فقعوا﴾: the fāʾ: connective (rābiṭa) for the answer of (إذا), and (قعوا): imperative verb and fāʿil; (له): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ساجدين﴾; and (ساجدين): ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:73-73.t: ﴿فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون﴾: the fāʾ: a conjunction; ﴿سجد الملائكة﴾: verb, fāʿil (agent); (كلهم): first tawkīd (emphasis), and the hāʾ: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (أجمعون): second tawkīd, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw.

muyesser-irab:74-74.t: ﴿إلا إبليس استكبر وكان من الكافرين﴾: (إلا): a particle of exception; (إبليس): the excepted (mustathnā), connected (muttaṣil) or disconnected (munqaṭiʿ); the clause ﴿استكبر﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (كان): conjoined to (استكبر), and the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); and ﴿من الكافرين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of (كان).

muyesser-irab:75-75.t:
﴿قال يا إبليس ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي﴾: (قال): past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) refers to Allah the Exalted; (يا): vocative particle; (إبليس): the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper name, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; (ما): an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿منعك﴾ is the khabar (predicate); (أن): a maṣdar-forming particle that puts into the accusative; (تسجد): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (أن) and what falls within its scope is in the position of the genitive by an omitted ﴿مِن﴾, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿منع﴾. ﴿لما خلقت بيدي﴾: the lām: a preposition; (ما): a relative noun, genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تسجد﴾; the clause ﴿خلقت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, and the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "I created him"; or (ما) is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is genitive by the lām, the maṣdar here meaning the thing created rather than the actual verbal noun; and (بيدي): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خلقت﴾.
﴿أستكبرت أم كنت من العالين﴾: the hamza: for interrogation, and the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) has dropped, being dispensed with. (استكبرت): verb and fāʿil; (أم): a connected (muttaṣila) conjunction; (كنت): (كان) is a deficient past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; and (من العالين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of ﴿كان﴾.

muyesser-irab:76-76.t: ﴿قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين﴾: (أنا): mubtadaʾ (subject); (خير): khabar (predicate); (منه): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خير﴾; the clause is the speech (maqūl) of the saying; (خلقتني): verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من نار): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خلق﴾; and ﴿خلقته من طين﴾: conjoined to ﴿خلقتني من نار﴾.

muyesser-irab:77-77.t: ﴿قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم﴾: (قال): past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو), referring to Allah the Exalted; (فاخرج): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and (اخرج) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you" (أنت); (منها): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اخرج﴾; (فإنك): the fāʾ gives the reason (taʿlīliyya), (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), the kāf is its noun, and (رجيم) is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:78-78.t: ﴿وإن عليك لعنتي إلى يوم الدين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (إن): a particle of emphasis that puts into the accusative; (عليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (إن); (لعنتي): the postponed noun of (إن), and the yāʾ: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلى يوم الدين): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "continuing"; and (الدين): muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:79-79.t: ﴿قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون﴾: (قال): past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring to Iblīs; ﴿فأنظرني﴾: the fāʾ: the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it discloses (afṣaḥat) an implied condition, its implied form being ﴿إذا جعلتني رجيمًا فأمهلني﴾ ("since You have made me accursed, then grant me respite"); (أنظرني): a verb of supplication, the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "You" (أنت), the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلى يوم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنظرني﴾; and the clause ﴿يبعثون﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it.

muyesser-irab:80-80.t: ﴿قال فإنك من المنظرين﴾: (قال): past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو); (فإنك): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters), and the kāf is its noun; and (من المنظرين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of (إن).

muyesser-irab:81-81.t: ﴿إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم﴾: (إلى يوم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿المنظرين﴾; (الوقت): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (المعلوم): a naʿt (adjective) of (الوقت), genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:82-82.t: ﴿قال فبعزتك لأغوينهم أجمعين﴾: (قال): verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the fāʾ: a conjunction; the bāʾ: a preposition and particle of oath; (عزتك): genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of oath; the lām: occurring in the answer to the oath; the clause ﴿أغوينهم﴾ has no grammatical position; (أغوينهم): imperfect verb, with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being "I" (أنا), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (أجمعين): tawkīd (emphasis).

muyesser-irab:83-83.t: ﴿إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين﴾: (إلا): a particle of exception; (عبادك): excepted (mustathnā); (منهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and (المخلصين): a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عبادك﴾.

muyesser-irab:84-84.t: ﴿قال فالحق والحق أقول﴾: (قال): verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو); the fāʾ: resumptive; (الحق): mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "is My oath" or "is from Me"; or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is the truth". The clause ﴿فالحق...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿والحق﴾: the wāw is parenthetical, and (الحق) is a fronted object of ﴿أقول﴾, i.e. "I say nothing but the truth". The clause ﴿الحق أقول﴾ is parenthetical between the oath and its answer, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:85-85.t: ﴿لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين﴾: the lām: occurring in the answer to the implied (muqaddar) oath; (أملأن): imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, the nūn being for emphasis, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I" (أنا); (جهنم): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أملأن﴾ is the answer to an implied oath, and the clause of the oath is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from (الحق), or resumptive by way of explanation (bayāniyya), with no grammatical position; (منك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أملأن﴾; ﴿ممن تبعك﴾: conjoined to ﴿منك﴾; the clause ﴿تبعك﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position. (منهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and (أجمعين): tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in (منهم), or of the kāf in (منك) and what is conjoined to it.

muyesser-irab:86-86.t: ﴿قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين﴾: (قل): imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); (ما): negating; (أسألكم): imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "I" (أنا), and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (عليه): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of (أجر) and was placed before it; (من): a connective (ṣila) preposition [i.e. redundant]; (أجر): genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position as the object of (أسألكم); the wāw: a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما): the Ḥijāzī negating «ما», which operates as «ليس» operates; (أنا): the noun of (ما); and ﴿من المتكلفين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of (ما). Or ﴿ما﴾ is negating, ﴿أنا﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ﴿من المتكلفين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:87-87.t: ﴿إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين﴾: (إن): negating; (هو): mubtadaʾ (subject); (إلا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ذكر): khabar (predicate) of (هو); and (للعالمين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of (ذكر).

muyesser-irab:88-88.t: ﴿ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين﴾: the wāw: a conjunction; the lām: the lām of oath; (تعلمن): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), because the nūn of emphasis is not directly attached to it, and the sign of its nominative is the presence of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw, also dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters: fāʿil (agent); the nūn: the heavy nūn of emphasis; (نبأه): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بعد): an accusative (manṣūb) adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تعلمن﴾; and (حين): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Ṣād
Meccan
﷽
﴿ص﴾: it has been read with fatḥa, with kasra, and with the dāl made quiescent (sukūn), and this last is the most common reading. Whoever makes it quiescent reads "صادْ" as one of the letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf al-hijāʾ), the dāl being treated as in a pause (waqf); we have explained this under His saying "الـم", I mean the chapter on the letters of the alphabet. Its meaning is "Allah is the Truthful (اَلصّادِقُ اللَّهُ)". It has also been said that it is an oath.
And His saying: ﴿والقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; the meaning is: "I swear by Ṣād, and by the Qur'an possessed of remembrance (أُقْسِمُ بِصادِ، وبِالقُرْآنِ ذِي الذَّكَرِ)". Whoever gives it fatḥa does so in two ways: it may be a fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn), and it may be in the sense of "recite Ṣād (اُتْلُ صادَ)", with "صادَ" being a name of the sūra, a diptote. Whoever gives it kasra does so in two ways: because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, or with kasra in the sense of "confront (ṣādi) the Qur'an with your deeds (صادِ القُرْآنَ بِعَمَلِكَ)", from your saying "صادى، يُصادِي" when one faces and matches [something]; one says "صادَيْتُهُ" when you have faced him.
The answer (jawāb) to His saying ﴿ص والقُرْآنِ﴾ is ﴿إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخاصُمُ أهْلِ النّارِ﴾ [Ṣād: 64]. Some people said: the answer is ﴿كَمْ أهْلَكْنا مِن قَبْلِهِمْ مِن قَرْنٍ﴾ [Ṣād: 3], its meaning being "لَكَمْ أهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهم مِن قَرْنٍ" (how many a generation We indeed destroyed before them); since the speech between the two became long, the lām was omitted.
The meaning of "والقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ" is: "possessed of mention and honour (ذِي الذِّكْرِ والشَّرَفِ)". It has also been said that "ذِي الذِّكْرِ" means: in it are mentioned the stories of the former and the later peoples, and what is needed concerning the lawful and the unlawful.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿أمْ لَهم مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: nothing of that is theirs. ﴿فَلْيَرْتَقُوا في الأسْبابِ﴾, that is: if they claim anything of that, then let them ascend by the means (asbāb) that would bring them to the heaven. It is also possible that it means "let them ascend by these means that have been mentioned, which none but Allah possesses".

zajjaj:11-11.t: Then Allah promised His Prophet, upon him be peace, victory over them, and said: ﴿جُنْدٌ ما هُنالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الأحْزابِ﴾. "ما" is redundant (laghw); the meaning is: "جُنْدٌ هُنالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الأحْزابِ" (a host there, routed, of the confederates).

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿وَفِرْعَوْنُ ذُو الأوْتادِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that Pharaoh had ropes and stakes on which people would perform for him «[Translator's note: «يُلْعَبُ لَهُ عَلَيْها», literally "played on for him".]».

zajjaj:3-3.t:
﴿فَنادَوْا ولاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ﴾: it has come in the exegesis (tafsīr): "and it was no time for calling out (وَلاتَ حِينَ نِداءٍ)". The people of the language said: "and it was no time for escape (وَلاتَ حِينَ مَنجًى)" and "no escaping (لا فَوْتَ)". One says "ناصَهُ، يَنُوصُهُ" when something has escaped him. In the exegesis, "لاتَ حِينَ نِداءٍ" means: "it was no time for a calling out that would save". It is also permissible to read "لاتَ حِينُ مَناصٍ" [with nominative], and the nominative is good.
The pause (waqf) on it is "لاتْ", with tāʾ; al-Kisāʾī pauses on it with hāʾ, "لاهْ", because he makes it the hāʾ of the feminine. The correct pause on it is with tāʾ, and this tāʾ is analogous to the tāʾ in the verb when you say "ذَهَبْتُ، وجَلَسْتُ", and in your saying "رَأيْتُ زَيْدًا ثُمَّتَ عَمْرًا" (I saw Zayd, then ʿAmr). So the tāʾ of particles is equivalent to the tāʾ of verbs, because in both places the tāʾ has entered upon something that is not declined (lā yuʿrab) and is not on the path of nouns.
If someone says: we treat it like their saying "كانَ مِنَ الأمْرِ ذَيْهْ" and "ذَيْهْ" (such-and-such happened), for this is a hāʾ in pause, and this is a hāʾ that has entered upon a noun which is not declined. «[Translator's note: the source gives no explicit reply to this objection.]»
They have also permitted the genitive (khafḍ), saying "لاتَ أوانٍ", and they recited, by Abū Zubayd:
؎طَلَبُوا صُلْحَنا ولاتَ أوانٍ ∗∗∗ فَأجَبْنا أنْ لَيْسَ حِينَ بَقاءِ
(They sought peace with us when it was no longer the time, so we answered that it was no time for survival.)
What Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] recited to us — and so he narrated it — was:
طَلَبُوا صُلْحَنا ولاتَ أوانٌ
and he mentioned that the kasra has also been narrated.
As for the accusative, it is on the basis that it [لات] operates as "لَيْسَ" operates; the meaning is "and the time is not a time of escape (وَلَيْسَ الوَقْتُ حِينَ مَناصٍ)". Whoever puts it in the nominative with it makes "حِينَ" the subject (ism) of "لَيْسَ" and implies the predicate (khabar), in the sense of "there is no time of escape for us (لَيْسَ حِينُ مَنجًى لَنا)". Whoever puts it in the genitive makes it indeclinable (mabnī) with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, just as they said "قَدِ لَكَ" and made it indeclinable on kasra.
The meaning is "it is not the time of our escape and the time of our deliverance (لَيْسَ حِينُ مَناصِنا وحِينُ مَنجانا)". So when he said "وَلاتَ أوانَ", he made it in the sense of "it is not the time of our [proper] time (لَيْسَ حِينَ أوانِنا)"; when the muḍāf ilayhi «[Translator's note: the source says «المضاف» (the muḍāf), though what is dropped from «أوانِنا» is the attached pronoun, i.e. the muḍāf ilayhi.]» was omitted, it was made indeclinable on the pause form, then given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The kasra is anomalous (shādhdh), resembling an error in the view of the Basrans; Sībawayh and al-Khalīl did not narrate the kasra, and what is followed in practice is the accusative and the nominative.
Al-Akhfash said that in "لاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ" its accusative is by "لا", just as you say "لا رَجُلَ في الدّارِ" (there is no man in the house), and the tāʾ entered for the feminine.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقالَ الكافِرُونَ هَذا ساحِرٌ كَذّابٌ﴾, up to His saying: ﴿لَشَيْءٌ عُجابٌ﴾ [Ṣād: 5], in the sense of "wondrous (عَجِيبٌ)". "عُجّابٌ" is also permissible, in the sense of "عَجِيبٌ"; one says "رَجُلٌ كَرِيمٌ، وكُرّامٌ، وكُرامٌ" (a generous man).
This is a report of what a group of the notables of Quraysh said: «When Abū Ṭālib fell ill with the illness in which he died, Abū Jahl ibn Hishām and a group of Quraysh came to visit him, and they complained to him about the Prophet ﷺ and said: He insults our gods and does such-and-such. So Abū Ṭālib reproached him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "I am calling you to a word by which the Arabs will submit to you, and by which the non-Arabs will pay you the jizya." Abū Jahl said: Yes, and ten [more], by way of mockery, meaning: we will say it and ten others with it. So he said: "There is no god but Allah (لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ)." They said: Has he made the gods one God? Then they rose and left their gathering, saying to one another: Walk on and be steadfast for your gods.»

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿وانْطَلَقَ المَلأُ مِنهم أنِ امْشُوا﴾: its meaning is: that is, "walk on (اِمْشُوا)"; its interpretation is: they say "walk on". It is also permissible [to understand it as] "وانْطَلَقَ المَلَأُ مِنهم بِأنِ امْشُوا" (the notables among them went forth with "walk on"), that is, with this saying.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿ما سَمِعْنا بِهَذا في المِلَّةِ الآخِرَةِ﴾ is also a report of what they said, that is: we have not heard of this in Christianity, nor in Judaism, nor in what we found our forefathers upon. ﴿إنْ هَذا إلا اخْتِلاقٌ﴾, that is: nothing but a fabricated saying (taqawwul).

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿أأُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِن بَيْنِنا﴾, that is: how has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us? That is: how has the Qur'an been sent down to Muhammad from among us?! ﴿بَلْ هم في شَكٍّ مِن ذِكْرِي﴾, that is: they say what they hold only while being in doubt.

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ﴾: if someone asks: what is the connection of ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ﴾ with His saying ﴿بَلْ هم في شَكٍّ مِن ذِكْرِي﴾ [Ṣād: 8], or with His saying ﴿أأُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ مِن بَيْنِنا﴾ [Ṣād: 8]? [The answer is that] this is evidence of their envy of the Prophet ﷺ for the favour of prophethood that Allah gave him. So Allah made known that sovereignty belongs to Him and the message is His to give; He chooses whom He wills, gives sovereignty to whom He wills, and sends down rain and mercy upon whom He wills. So He said: ﴿أمْ عِنْدَهم خَزائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ﴾, that is: they do not have that.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿ما لَها مِن فَواقٍ﴾, and "فُواقٍ", with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the fāʾ, that is: "it has no return (ما لَها مِن رُجُوعٍ)". "اَلْفُواقُ" is the interval between two milkings of the she-camel, and it too is derived from [the sense of] returning, because the milk returns to the udder between the two milkings. "أفاقَ مِن مَرَضِهِ" (he recovered from his illness) is from this, that is, he returned to health; so "الفَواقُ" is from this as well.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
﴿وَقالُوا رَبَّنا عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا﴾: "اَلْقِطُّ" is the share (naṣīb). Its origin is the written sheet (ṣaḥīfa) in which something due to reach a person is written for him. Al-Aʿshā said:
؎وَلا المَلِكُ النُّعْمانُ يَوْمَ لَقِيتُهُ ∗∗∗ بِغِبْطَتِهِ يُعْطِي القُطُوطَ ويَأْفِقُ
(Nor King al-Nuʿmān, on the day I met him in his prosperity, giving out written grants and bestowing generously.)
"يَأْفِقُ" means: he gives in excess (yufḍil). This is the explanation of their saying "عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا", and it is like their saying: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32], to the end of the verse. It has also been said that when they heard that the believer will be given his book in his right hand and the disbeliever will be given his book in his left hand, so that the believer is made happy and the disbeliever is ruined, they said: "Our Lord, hasten for us our share (عَجِّلْ لَنا قِطَّنا)".
The derivation of "اَلْقِطُّ" is from "قَطَطْتُ", that is, "I cut (قَطَعْتُ)"; and likewise the share is simply a piece (qiṭʿa) of a thing.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ ذا الأيْدِ﴾: "possessed of strength (ذا القُوَّةِ)". His strength in worship was the most complete strength: he used to fast one day and break his fast one day, and that is the most severe fasting, and he used to pray half the night.
﴿إنَّهُ أوّابٌ﴾: "one who returns to Allah often (رَجّاعٌ إلى اللَّهِ كَثِيرًا)". "اَلْآيِبُ" is the one who returns, and "اَلْأوّابُ" is the one who returns often.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿إنّا سَخَّرْنا الجِبالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِالعَشِيِّ والإشْراقِ﴾: "اَلْإشْراقُ" is the rising of the sun and its shining. One says "شَرِقَتِ الشَّمْسُ" when the sun rises, and "أشْرَقَتْ" when it shines. It has also been said that "شَرِقَتْ" and "أشْرَقَتْ", when it rises, have one meaning; but the first is more common.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿والطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً كُلٌّ لَهُ أوّابٌ﴾: the mountains used to repeat the glorification (tasbīḥ) back, and so did the birds. It is possible that the hāʾ [in لَهُ] refers to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, that is: "all glorify Allah — the birds, the mountains and David glorify Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and repeat the glorification". And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that "كُلٌّ لَّهُ أوّابٌ" means: all of them repeat the glorification with David, answering him; whenever he glorified, the mountains and the birds glorified with him.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
﴿وَشَدَدْنا مُلْكَهُ﴾: "وَشَدَّدْنا" [with doubled dāl] is also permissible, but I do not know anyone who read it so. Its meaning is "We strengthened his kingdom". Part of the strengthening of his kingdom was that his sanctuary (miḥrāb) was guarded every night by thirty-three thousand men.
It has also been said that a man sought his help against another man, claiming that he had taken cattle from him. The defendant denied it, so David asked the claimant for evidence (bayyina), but he could not produce it. Then David saw in his sleep that Allah was commanding him to kill the defendant. David held back and said: it is a dream. Then revelation came to him after that that he should kill him. So he summoned him and informed him that Allah had commanded him to kill him. The defendant said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has not taken me to task for this sin; rather, I killed this man's father treacherously. So David killed him. That was among the things by which Allah exalted him and strengthened his kingdom.
﴿وَآتَيْناهُ الحِكْمَةَ وفَصْلَ الخِطابِ﴾: it has been said about this: that he judges by evidence and oath. It has been said about "فَصْلَ الخِطابِ": that he distinguishes between truth and falsehood. And it has been said: [it is the phrase] "أمّا بَعْدُ" (as for what follows), and he was the first to say "أمّا بَعْدُ".

zajjaj:21-21.t:
﴿وَهَلْ أتاكَ نَبَأُ الخَصْمِ إذْ تَسَوَّرُوا المِحْرابَ﴾: "اَلْمِحْرابُ" is the highest room in the house, and likewise it is the highest place in the mosque; "اَلْمِحْرابُ" here is like an upper chamber (ghurfa). The poet said:
؎رَبَّةُ مِحْرابٍ إذا جِئْتُها ∗∗∗ لَمْ ألْقَها أوْ أرْتَقِي سُلَّما
(Mistress of an upper chamber: when I come to her, I cannot meet her unless I climb a ladder.)
"تَسَوَّرُوا" (they climbed over the wall) indicates height.
He said "اَلْخَصْمِ", whose form is the form of the singular, while "تَسَوَّرُوا" is the form of the plural, because your saying "خَصْمٌ" is suitable for the singular, the dual and the plural, the masculine and the feminine. One says "هَذا خَصْمٌ", "هي خَصْمٌ", "هُما خَصْمٌ" and "هم خَصْمٌ". It is suitable for all of that only because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun): you say "خَصَمْتُهُ، أخْصِمُهُ، خَصْمًا". The meaning is "they two are parties to a dispute (هُما ذَوا خَصْمٍ)" and "they are parties to a dispute (هم ذَوُو خَصْمٍ)". If you say "خُصُومٌ", it is permissible, just as you say "هُما عَدْلٌ" and "هُما ذَوا عَدْلٍ"; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَأشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 2]. So the meaning of "هُما عَدْلٌ" is "هُما ذَوا عَدْلٍ" (they two are possessors of justice).
Whatever verbal nouns you have used to describe nouns may be kept singular even if you describe a plural with them, and may be kept masculine even if you describe a feminine with them. You say "هو رِضًى" (he is pleasing), "هُما رِضًى", and likewise "هَذِهِ رِضًى".

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إذْ دَخَلُوا عَلى داوُدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنهُمْ﴾: because they came to him not by the way litigants come, not at their [usual] time, and at a time in which David did not permit anyone to enter upon him; so he found that strange and was alarmed. In fact, two angels were sent to him, who took the form of two men disputing with each other.
﴿قالُوا لا تَخَفْ خَصْمانِ بَغى بَعْضُنا عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾: the reading is with the nominative, and what makes "خَصْمانِ" nominative is "نَحْنُ" (we); the meaning is "we are two litigants (نَحْنُ خَصْمانِ)". Had the speech been "لا تَخَفْ خَصْمَيْنِ بَغى بَعْضُنا عَلى بَعْضٍ", it would be permissible, in the sense of "we have come to you as two litigants (أتَيْناكَ خَصْمَيْنِ)", because he found their coming strange, whereas the coming of litigants was something he was very much used to.
﴿فاحْكم بَيْنَنا بِالحَقِّ ولا تُشْطِطْ﴾, that is: "do not be unjust (لا تَجُرْ)"; one says "أشَطَّ، يُشِطُّ" when one is unjust. It is also read "لا تَشْطُطْ", in the sense of "do not go far from the truth", and likewise "لا تَشْطِطْ", with kasra on the ṭāʾ and fatḥa on the tāʾ, whose meaning is like the meaning of the previous one. The poet said:
؎تَشُطُّ غَدًا دارُ جِيرانِنا ∗∗∗ ولَلدّارُ بَعْدَ غَدٍ أبْعَدُ
(Tomorrow the abode of our neighbours will be far, and the abode the day after tomorrow farther still.)
﴿واهْدِنا إلى سَواءِ الصِّراطِ﴾: to the straight course of the road, that is, "the road of truth".

zajjaj:23-23.t:
﴿تِسْعٌ وتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً﴾: He used the ewe (naʿja) as a metonym (kināya) for a woman. Al-Aʿshā said:
؎فَرَمَيْتُ غُفْلَةَ عَيْنِهِ عَنْ شاتِهِ ∗∗∗ فَأصَبْتُ حَبَّةَ قَلْبِها وطِحالَها
(I shot when his eye was heedless of his ewe, and struck the core of her heart and her spleen.)
By "the ewe (al-shāt)" here he meant the woman.
﴿فَقالَ أكْفِلْنِيها﴾, that is: make me the one who takes charge of her, and you give her up. ﴿وَعَزَّنِي في الخِطابِ﴾: he overcame me in the dispute, that is, he was stronger than me in argument.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
﴿قالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إلى نِعاجِهِ﴾: the meaning is "by his asking for your ewe so that he may add it to his ewes (بِسُؤالِهِ نَعْجَتَكَ لِيَضُمَّها إلى نِعاجِهِ)". ﴿وَإنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الخُلَطاءِ﴾: of the partners; you say "فُلانٌ خَلِيطِي، وشَرِيكِي" (so-and-so is my associate, my partner) with one meaning. ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ وقَلِيلٌ ما هُمْ﴾, that is: "few are they (قَلِيلٌ هُمْ)".
And His saying: ﴿وَظَنَّ داوُدُ أنَّما فَتَنّاهُ﴾, to the end of the verse. It is also read without doubling, "فَتَناهُ", by which the two angels are meant «[Translator's note: i.e. "that the two of them tried him".]». The meaning of "ظَنَّ" is: he was certain, except that it is not the certainty of eyewitnessing; for eyewitnessing, only "عَلِمَ" is said.
﴿فاسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُ وخَرَّ راكِعًا وأنابَ﴾: he remained forty days prostrating, not raising his head, asking Allah's forgiveness for his sin, except for an obligatory prayer and what he could not do without, and his tears did not cease.
It is narrated in the exegesis that the cause of the story of David and the two angels was that Iblīs — may Allah's wrath be upon him — appeared to him in the form of a bird of gold, which landed near him. He went to it to take it, but it moved away; he pursued it, and whenever he was about to reach it, it moved away. While following the bird, David caught sight of a woman bathing, and she caught sight of him, so she covered herself with her hair until it concealed her. It is said that she was the wife of Ūriyā ibn Ḥannān. It is narrated that he wrote to the commander of his army to put Ūriyā in the front in a war that was taking place; so he put him forward and he was killed, and David married her.
It is narrated that ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Whoever says that David, upon him be peace, committed anything suspicious with this woman, I will flog him one hundred and sixty lashes, because whoever falsely accuses someone other than a prophet is flogged eighty lashes, and whoever falsely accuses a prophet is flogged one hundred and sixty lashes."
It was in the exegesis that David wished that Ūriyā would perish so that David could marry his wife. This — and Allah knows best — was only on David's part by way of wishing that it would happen for him without his intending it or working towards the man's death, and Allah counted it as a sin against him because of what he wished. It is also possible that he wrote that this man should be put forward in front of the Ark (al-tābūt) because of his valour and bravery in war, hoping for his sufficiency [in battle], and it happened along with that that he was struck down, and thereby his wife became lawful for him. So he was reproached for loving the wife of a man who had no other, while David had ninety-nine wives; and that was among the sins of the prophets. So when he went to great lengths in repentance and exerted himself in beseeching Allah for pardon, until he almost destroyed himself repenting and clearing himself before Allah of his sin — «[Translator's note: the main clause of this sentence is not completed in the source.]» — and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has described that, saying: ﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا داوُدَ ذا الأيْدِ إنَّهُ أوّابٌ﴾ [Ṣād: 17]. And the saying of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, "May Allah bless David and have mercy on him", indicates the soundness of this interpretation; and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:26-26.t:
﴿إنّا جَعَلْناكَ خَلِيفَةً في الأرْضِ﴾: on this basis it became permissible to call the caliphs "the vicegerents of Allah on earth (خُلَفاءُ اللَّهِ في الأرْضِ)". ﴿فاحْكم بَيْنَ النّاسِ بِالحَقِّ﴾, that is: by the judgement of Allah, since you are His vicegerent.
And His saying: ﴿بِما نَسُوا يَوْمَ الحِسابِ﴾, that is: by their abandoning work for this Day they became like those who forget, even though they were being warned and reminded.

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾, to the end of the verse: Allah made known to them that He will punish them for [this] supposition (ẓann); and likewise: ﴿وَظَنُّوا أنَّهم إلَيْنا لا يُرْجَعُونَ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 39]. This was said to them only because they denied the resurrection. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿أفَحَسِبْتُمْ أنَّما خَلَقْناكم عَبَثًا وأنَّكم إلَيْنا لا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 115]: if there were no return, there would be no distinction between the wicked and the righteous. After this: ﴿أمْ نَجْعَلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ كالمُفْسِدِينَ في الأرْضِ﴾ [Ṣād: 28], to the end of the verse. Then He said: ﴿كِتابٌ أنْـزَلْناهُ إلَيْكَ مُبارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آياتِهِ﴾ [Ṣād: 29]; the meaning is: "this is a Book (هَذا كِتابٌ), so that they may reflect on its verses", that is, so that they may think about its verses and about the ends (adbār) of their affairs, that is, their consequences. ﴿وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الألْبابِ﴾ [Ṣād: 29], that is: those possessed of intellects.

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿نِعْمَ العَبْدُ إنَّهُ أوّابٌ﴾: the meaning is: "an excellent servant is Solomon (نِعْمَ العَبْدُ سُلَيْمانُ); he is one who turns [to Allah], often returning".

zajjaj:31-31.t:
﴿إذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالعَشِيِّ الصّافِناتُ الجِيادُ﴾: "اَلصّافِناتُ" are horses standing. The people of the language and the people of exegesis said: "اَلصّافِنُ" is the one standing that bends one of its forelegs or one of its hind legs so that it stands on the tip of its hoof (sunbuk), which is the edge of the hoof; so three of its legs are in contact with the ground, and of one leg only the edge of the hoof touches the ground. The poet said:
؎ألِفَ الصُّفُونَ فَلا يَزالُ كَأنَّهُ ∗∗∗ مِمّا يَقُومُ عَلى الثَّلاثِ كَسِيرا
(He grew used to standing on three legs, so he still seems, from standing on three, as if he were lame.)
Some of them said: "اَلصّافِنُ" is the one standing, whether it bends one of its legs or does not bend it. Horses mostly stand — when they stand — in the ṣāfin posture, because it is as though they alternate between their legs.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
﴿فَقالَ إنِّي أحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي حَتّى تَوارَتْ بِالحِجابِ﴾: "اَلْخَيْرُ" here means horses (al-khayl). The Prophet ﷺ named Zayd al-Khayl "Zayd al-Khayr". Horses were called "اَلْخَيْرَ" (the good) only because «good is tied to the forelocks of horses», as has come in the ḥadīth.
These horses had come to Solomon from the spoils of an army of his, and he became preoccupied with reviewing them until the sun set and the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr) escaped him.
The people of the language said: "حَتّى تَوارَتْ بِالحِجابِ" means the sun, though the sun has not been mentioned. In this matter I do not reckon that they gave the thinking its due, because in the verse there is an indication pointing to the sun, namely His saying: ﴿إذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالعَشِيِّ﴾ [Ṣād: 31], and "al-ʿashiyy" has the meaning of "after the sun's decline from the meridian"; [so it is] "until the sun was hidden behind the veil (حَتّى تَوارَتِ الشَّمْسُ بِالحِجابِ)". An implied pronoun (iḍmār) is not permissible unless there has been a mention, or an indication of a mention that stands in place of the mention.
Solomon, because of the awe he inspired, was such that no one dared to approach him to alert him to the time of a prayer. I do not know whether the afternoon prayer was obligatory at that time or not; but his reviewing of the horses occupied him until a time passed in which Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is remembered.
The meaning of "أحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الخَيْرِ" is: I preferred the love of good things (al-khayr) to the remembrance of Allah.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
﴿رُدُّوها عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحًا بِالسُّوقِ والأعْناقِ﴾: "اَلْمَسْحُ" here, according to what has come in the exegesis, is cutting; it is narrated that he struck their legs and their necks. "سُوقٌ" is the plural of "ساقٌ" (leg), like "دارٌ" and "دُورٌ". Solomon would not have struck their necks unless Allah had permitted that, because He does not make repentance from a sin by means of a great sin.
Some people said: he wiped their necks and legs with water and with his hand. But this — I mean his wiping them with water — does not follow from their having distracted him. Those people only said that because killing them was, in their view, reprehensible; but what Allah permits is not reprehensible. It is possible that that was permitted for Solomon in his time and is forbidden at this time.
Mālik holds that the flesh of horses, mules and donkeys should not be eaten, because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والخَيْلَ والبِغالَ والحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوها وزِينَةً﴾ [al-Naḥl: 8], while He said about camels: ﴿لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنها ومِنها تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 79].

zajjaj:34-34.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنّا سُلَيْمانَ﴾: "فَتَنّا" means "We tested". ﴿وَألْقَيْنا عَلى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that Solomon had a son, and he feared the devils for him, because the devils expected relief from the state they were in through Solomon's death; they said: if a child of his survives, we shall not be freed from what we are in. So he nourished him in the clouds out of concern for him, and he died, and a body was cast upon his throne. It is possible that this was a requital for his sin, and it is possible that it means Allah bereaved him of his child.
Most of what has come in the exegesis is that "جَسَدًا" here is "a devil (شَيْطانٌ)", and that Solomon had been commanded not to marry any woman except from the Children of Israel, but he married from others a woman who worshipped other than Allah. So Allah punished him by stripping him of his kingdom. His kingdom was in his ring, and on entering the bath he handed it to a devil — it has come in the exegesis that he was called "Ṣakhr" — who threw it into the sea. So he remained forty days wandering in the land until he found the ring in the belly of a fish. A devil had taken on his form and sat in his place, and his command was carried out in everything in which Solomon's command had been carried out, except Solomon's wives, until Allah restored his kingdom to him. He said: ﴿فَغَفَرْنا لَهُ ذَلِكَ﴾ [Ṣād: 25], that is, that sin; ﴿وَإنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾ [Ṣād: 25]: a good place of return. «[Translator's note: the words quoted here, with the reference [Ṣād: 25], occur in the Qur'an at Ṣād 25 about David; the closing words also occur at Ṣād 40 about Solomon. The text is translated as written.]»

zajjaj:35-35.t: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لا يَنْبَغِي لأحَدٍ مِن بَعْدِي إنَّكَ أنْتَ الوَهّابُ﴾, that is: "grant me a kingdom in which there is a sign indicating my prophethood, such as befits no one after me among human beings who are not prophets, so that it is a sign for him «[Translator's note: i.e. for Solomon.]» indicating that You have forgiven me and restored my prophethood to me". The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿فَسَخَّرْنا لَهُ الرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأمْرِهِ رُخاءً حَيْثُ أصابَ﴾ [Ṣād: 36]. "رُخاءً" means gentle; it has also been said: it blows at his command, not violent, as he likes. ﴿حَيْثُ أصابَ﴾ [Ṣād: 36]: the consensus of the exegetes and the people of the language is that it means wherever he wished; its literal sense is "he aimed (قَصَدَ)". Likewise your saying to the one who answers a question "أصَبْتَ" (you are right), that is, "you aimed [correctly] (قَصَدْتَ)" and did not miss the answer.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
﴿والشَّياطِينَ كُلَّ بَنّاءٍ وغَوّاصٍ﴾: "اَلشَّياطِينَ" is conjoined (nasaq) to "اَلرِّيحَ". His saying "كُلَّ بَنّاءٍ وغَوّاصٍ" indicates that it is of the devils; the meaning is "and We subjected to him every builder among the devils, and every diver (وَسَخَّرْنا لَهُ كُلَّ بِنّاءٍ مِنَ الشَّياطِينِ، وكُلَّ غَوّاصٍ)". Those who built ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ ما يَشاءُ مِن مَحارِيبَ وتَماثِيلَ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 13], and those who dived brought out ornaments for him from the sea.
﴿وَآخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ في الأصْفادِ﴾ [Ṣād: 38]: the rebellious ones among the jinn, the devils, were subjected to him so that he bound them together in fetters. "اَلْأصْفادُ" are chains of iron. Everything you have bound firmly with iron or anything else, you have "صَفَدْتَهُ"; and everyone to whom you have given a lavish gift, you have "أصْفَدْتَهُ", as though you had given him something by which he is tied [to you] — just as you say to one who acquires wealth as capital to keep: "you have acquired a good holding (قَدِ اتَّخَذْتَ عُقْدَةً جَيِّدَةً)".

zajjaj:39-39.t:
﴿هَذا عَطاؤُنا فامْنُنْ﴾, that is: release whomever you wish of them.
﴿أوْ أمْسِكْ﴾: or detain whomever you wish, and there is no reckoning against you for detaining him. It is possible that "عَطاؤُنا" is what We have given you of wealth, abundance and kingdom; ﴿فامْنُنْ﴾, that is: give from it; ﴿أوْ أمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾: without any favour held over you; or, if you wish, "بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ" means: without requital.

zajjaj:41-41.t:
﴿واذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا أيُّوبَ إذْ نادى رَبَّهُ أنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطانُ بِنُصْبٍ وعَذابٍ﴾: "عَبْدَنا" is accusative because the action falls upon it, and "أيُّوبَ" is a badal (substitute) for "عَبْدَنا", because "أيُّوبَ" is the proper name, and a proper name cannot be a naʿt (adjective); it can only be an explanatory badal.
"بِنُصْبٍ", and "نَصَبٍ" with fatḥa on the nūn and the ṣād, and "نُصْبٍ" with ḍamma on the nūn, have one meaning. It has been read "بِنُصْبٍ" with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād, and it has been read with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād; and "وَنَصَبٍ", with fatḥa on the nūn and the ṣād, is equivalent to "نُصْبٍ" with ḍamma on the nūn. "اَلنُّصْبُ" and "اَلنَّصَبُ" are like "اَلرُّشْدُ" and "اَلرَّشَدُ", "اَلْبُخْلُ" and "اَلْبَخَلُ", "اَلْعُرْبُ" and "اَلْعَرَبُ". "اَلنَّصْبُ", with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād, is on the original pattern of the maṣdar (verbal noun); and "اَلنُّصْبُ" and "اَلنَّصَبُ" are in the sense of "نَصَبْتُ، نَصْبًا، ونُصْبًا، ونَصْبًا", on the original pattern of the maṣdar.
The meaning of "بِنُصْبٍ وعَذابٍ" is: with harm in my body and torment in my wealth and my family. It may also be: with harm in my body and torment in it. It is narrated that Job, upon him be peace, remained afflicted for seven years, with worms crawling from his body, and he called upon his Lord: ﴿أنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ وأنْتَ أرْحَمُ الرّاحِمِينَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 83].

zajjaj:42-42.t: ﴿ارْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ﴾: the meaning is "We said to him: strike with your foot (قُلْنا لَهُ: اُرْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ)", meaning "tread the ground with your foot". So he trod the ground lightly once, and a spring gushed forth for him; he washed in it, and the disease left the outside of his body. Then he trod a second time, and water gushed forth and he drank from it, and it washed the disease from the inside of his body.

zajjaj:43-43.t: ﴿وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ أهْلَهُ ومِثْلَهم مَعَهُمْ﴾: it has been said: "وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ أهْلَهُ" means We gave him in the Hereafter the reward for losing them, and gave him in this world the like of them. It has also been said: his family was brought back to life for him, and the like of them was given to him. ﴿رَحْمَةً مِنّا﴾: "رَحْمَةً" is accusative, a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). ﴿وَذِكْرى لأُولِي الألْبابِ﴾: for those possessed of intellects. The meaning of "وَذِكْرى لِأُولِي الألْبابِ" is: when an intelligent person is afflicted, he remembers the affliction of Job and is patient.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
﴿وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثًا﴾: the meaning is "and We said: take in your hand (وَقُلْنا: خُذْ بِيَدِكَ)". "اَلضِّغْثُ" is a bundle of grass, or of sweet basil, or something similar.
It has come in the exegesis that Job's wife said to him: "If only you would seek nearness to the devil and slaughter a young she-goat for him." He said: "Not even a handful of dust." And he swore that, when he was healed, he would flog her a hundred lashes. Allah was grateful to her for her service to him, so He made the expiation of his oath that he should take a bundle containing a hundred twigs and strike her a single blow. People have differed: some said this was particular to Job, upon him be peace, and others said it applies to all people.
﴿أوّابٌ﴾: one who returns often to Allah.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
﴿واذْكُرْ عِبادَنا إبْراهِيمَ وإسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ﴾: whoever says "عِبادَنا" makes "إبْراهِيمَ وإسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ" a badal (substitute) for "عِبادَنا"; and whoever reads "عَبَدْنا" «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the singular reading «عَبْدَنا» is meant, as the following sentence shows.]» makes "إبْراهِيمَ" alone the badal, and makes "إسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ" conjoined (ʿaṭf) to His saying "عَبْدَنا".
And His saying: ﴿أُولِي الأيْدِي﴾: it has also been read "اَلْأيْدِ", without yāʾ. The meaning of "أُولِي الأيْدِي" is: possessed of strength in worship. ﴿والأبْصارِ﴾, that is: they are possessed of insight in what brings near to Allah. One may say of a people: "they have hands (أيْدِي) over these", that is, "they have power over them". The poet said:
؎اِعْمَدْ لِما تَعْلُو فَما لَكَ بِالَّذِي ∗∗∗ لا تَسْتَطِيعُ مِنَ الأُمُورِ يَدانِ
(Aim for what you can master, for you have no two hands for matters beyond your power.)
That is: aim for what you can overcome, and do not aim for that in which you will be overcome, that is, for you have no strength [for it]. Whoever reads "أُولِي الأيْدِ", without yāʾ, its meaning is from "اَلتَّأْيِيدُ" (support), and strengthening for something.

zajjaj:46-46.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنّا أخْلَصْناهم بِخالِصَةٍ ذِكْرى الدّارِ﴾: it is also read "بِخالِصَةِ ذِكْرى الدّارِ", with "خالِصَةِ" in genitive construct (iḍāfa) with "ذِكْرى". Whoever reads with tanwīn makes "ذِكْرى الدّارِ" a badal (substitute) for "خالِصَةٍ", and the meaning is "We purified them by the remembrance of the Abode (إنّا أخْلَصْناهم بِذِكْرى الدّارِ)". The meaning of "اَلدّارُ" here is the abode of the Hereafter.
Its interpretation admits two aspects. One of them: "إنّا أخْلَصْناهم" — We made them purely Ours, by making them remind [people] of the abode of the Hereafter and make them renounce this world; and such is the way of the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them. And it may be [that it is] by their frequently remembering the Hereafter and returning to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

zajjaj:47-47.t: ﴿وَإنَّهم عِنْدَنا لَمِنَ المُصْطَفَيْنَ الأخْيارِ﴾, that is: those whom Allah took as His chosen elite; He purified them from all impurities and freed them from them.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
And His saying: ﴿واذْكُرْ إسْماعِيلَ واليَسَعَ وذا الكِفْلِ﴾: it is also read "واللَّيْسَعَ وذا الكِفْلِ". He had taken responsibility (takaffala) for the work of a righteous man; it is said that that man used to pray a hundred prayers every day, and when the righteous man died, Dhū al-Kifl took responsibility for his work and used to do his work. It is also said that Dhū al-Kifl took responsibility for the affair of some prophets and saved them from being killed, so he was named "Dhū al-Kifl".
﴿وَكُلٌّ مِنَ الأخْيارِ﴾: the meaning is "and all of these who have been mentioned are among the best". "اَلْأخْيارُ" is the plural of "خَيِّرٌ", and "أخْيارٌ" is like "مَيِّتٌ" and "أمْواتٌ".

zajjaj:49-49.t:
﴿هَذا ذِكْرٌ وإنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: this is an honour and a fine mention by which they will be remembered forever, and in addition to that they will have a good place of return (maʾāb), that is, a good return: they are mentioned with praise in this world and return in the Hereafter to Allah's forgiveness. Then He explained how good that return is, saying: ﴿جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الأبْوابُ﴾ [Ṣād: 50]. "جَنّاتِ" is a badal (substitute) for "لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ".
The meaning of "مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الأبْوابُ" is: that is, [the gates] of them (مِنها). Some of them said: [it means] "with their gates opened for them (مُفَتَّحَةً لَهم أبْوابُها)", and the meaning is the same; but in terms of Arabic grammatical analysis (taqdīr), "the gates of them (اَلْأبْوابُ مِنها)" is better than making the alif and lām a substitute for the hāʾ and alif, because the meaning of the alif and lām is in no way the meaning of the hāʾ and alif: the hāʾ and alif are a noun (ism), while the alif and lām entered for definiteness, and a particle that came for a meaning is not substituted for a noun, nor does it stand in for it; that is impossible.

zajjaj:52-52.t: ﴿وَعِنْدَهم قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ أتْرابٌ﴾: He means houris who have restrained their glances to their husbands, so they do not look at anyone else. ﴿أتْرابٌ﴾: peers; ﴿وَكَواعِبَ أتْرابًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 33], that is, their ages are one, and they are at the height of youth and beauty.

zajjaj:53-53.t: ﴿هَذا ما تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ الحِسابِ﴾, that is: for a day on which every soul will be recompensed for what it did. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the bliss of the people of Paradise does not end, saying: ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَرِزْقُنا ما لَهُ مِن نَفادٍ﴾ [Ṣād: 54], that is, it has no ending.

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿هَذا وإنَّ لِلطّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ﴾: the meaning is "the matter is this (اَلْأمْرُ هَذا)"; so "هَذا" is nominative, the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). Or, if you wish, "هَذا" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted. And "جَهَنَّمَ" [Ṣād: 56] is a badal (substitute) for "شَرَّ مَآبٍ", that is, an evil place of return.

zajjaj:57-57.t:
﴿هَذا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وغَسّاقٌ﴾: [غَسّاقٌ is read] with the sīn doubled and undoubled. "حَمِيمٌ" is nominative in two respects.
